LD 13: An Act to Provide Funds Necessary for the Production and Delivery of Election Materials by the Secretary of State and to Reconvene the Working Group to Study Polling Places at Schools

Good morning Senator Hickman and Representative Supica,
My name is Al Cleveland. I am here today as the Advocacy Director of the League of Women Voters of Maine.
The League is testifying in support of LD 13.
The League of Women Voters of Maine is a nonpartisan political organization that has been working for over 100
years to encourage informed and active participation in government, to increase understanding of major public
policy issues, and to influence public policy through education and advocacy. We never support or oppose any
political party or candidate.
The Office of the Secretary of State requires reliable, sustainable funding to print ballots and election materials. This bill would provide the necessary changes to the Office of the SOS to consistently fund the cost of election
materials.
lt should never be an issue whether a policy initiative advances simply because we don't have the money to print an extra ballot page: the fiscal note for ballots or ballot pages should not be the determinant. For example, when
the League was working to pass semi-open primaries, in 2021, the bill ended up with a fiscal note because if more people vote, we'd have to print more ballots. The Office of the SOS should not be put in a position to question or weigh the impact of its support for a bill because the length of the ballots or number of voters would increase costs. More specifically, it's a perverse disadvantage for a bill to have as a perceived downside that it aims to increase voter participation. Nor should the Office be required to make up these ballot expenses after
the fact, depending on how many candidates or questions appear on the ballot in any given year, or based on
anticipated voter turnout. Requiring the Office to trade these expenses off against other budget needs continually short-changes the needs of the Elections Division to perform critical functions.
The League supports a formal working group to study the role of polling places at schools. Schools are often
centrally located in communities, close to where voters live, making them ideal polling places. However, we
understand the impact of school closure and the hardship this imposes on teachers and parents. Polling places are pillars of our community and deserve the deep attention that a working group can bring to bear.
Thank you for the opportunity to testify. I would be happy to answer any questions from the Committee.

Senator Hickman, Representative Supica, and the distinguished members of the Veterans and Legal Affairs Committee,
Mainers For Modern Elections would like to share our support for LD 13.
Mainers for Modern Elections is a non-partisan coalition of advocacy groups that believes a functioning democracy requires easy access to the ballot for eligible voters, especially from marginalized voting populations; strong voter protections; and confidence in a secure, modern, representative, and well-resourced elections system. The coalition advocates for statutorily protected voting rights, structural democracy reforms that expand voter access, and investment in and modernization of election administration and implementation. We pursue these policies through direct and grassroots advocacy and by educating and providing resources to public officials and coalition members.
LD 13 addresses an ongoing challenge that jeopardizes Maine's Election Division's ability to complete vital tasks. Printing ballots and election materials is a foundational component to Maine's election process. The Office of the Secretary of State requires reliable funding to ensure a smooth completion of this basic and essential step. This bill establishes a consistent fund for the cost of election materials allowing the Office of the Secretary of State of State to focus their efforts on other points of the election process.
A particularly long ballot or a higher-than-expected turnout of citizens casting ballots will increase election costs, leaving the Office of the Secretary of State to make up these ballot expenses from other funds. Requiring the Office of the Secretary of State to make cuts in other approved budget areas to cover these costs continually short-changes the needs of the Elections Division.
Mainers for Modern Election supports a formal working group to study school polling places. Schools are often centrally located in communities, close to where voters live, making them ideal polling places. However, we understand the impact of school closure and the hardship this imposes on teachers and parents. Polling places are pillars of our community and deserve the deep attention that a working group can bring to bear.
Thank you for the opportunity to submit this testimony.

Position:

SUPPORT

The Maine Town & City Clerks' Association is in support of LD 13 and we thank you for the
opportunity to outline our points for your Committee.

FUNDING OF ELECTIONS: Members expressed strong support for adequately funding the Secretary of State for the
production and delivery of election materials to municipal clerks. Timely receipt of these
materials by municipal clerks helps make the administration of elections more manageable.

RECONVENING THE WORKING GROUP TO STUDY POLLING PLACES AT SCHOOLS:
Since many municipalities use schools as their polling places, members expressed support
for continuing to explore the concerns about security of students and school staff, election staff and voters. Clerks noted that having students and school staff present while voting is taking place at that school presents significant challenges to both school administrators and
election administrators. Discussion of these issues with the listed stakeholders should
provide amenable recommendations.

The Maine Town & City Clerks' Association appreciates the opportunity to share its testimony with the Committee. Should any questions arise, please feel free to contact me at

Testimony of Shenna Bellows, Secretary of State Department of the Secretary of State

January 27, 2025

Testifying in favor
L.D. 13 "An Act to Provide Funds Necessary for the Production and Delivery of Election Materials by
the Secretary of State and to Reconvene the Working Group to Study Polling Places at Schools"
Senator Hickman, Representative Supica and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans
and Legal Affairs, my name is Shenna Bellows and I am the Secretary of State and the chief elections
officer. I am speaking today in support of L.D. 13.

Section one addresses the reoccurring challenges we see within elections regarding funding. Supply
chain and staffing issues have increased the cost of materials for ballots, printing, postage, and other election costs in addition to the delivery of such materials, which in turn has increased the cost of statewide elections dramatically in recent years. Indeed, since Senator Hickman introduced a similar
bill last legislature, we have seen further increases. The second ballot in the November 2024 election --~
the referendum ballot -- cost $408,431.41. The detailed quote from the printer is included at the end of
this testimony.
Unfortunately, while a fiscal note of sorts is included on all bills and bonds that may go to the voters,
that is not the type of fiscal note that results in any funds being appropriated to a Department. I learned
this when we reached out to the Comptroller's office last sunnner for the funds from each of those
pieces of legislation, so that we could pay for the printing and shipping of ballots. We were told no
funds would be coming. Instead, we were forced to once again get creative with how we paid our bills, and we made it work, but this is why I appeared before this committee and the Appropriations and
Financial Affairs Committee last week requesting this funding.

L.D. 13 offers a new path forward for future years. Establishing a fund to receive ongoing
appropriations and allowing any remaining balances to be carried forward, will ensure predictability
and stability when it comes to election material expenses incurred, instead of this office repeatedly needing to ask for supplemental appropriations to pay for elections we are legally required to hold.
Additionally, having spoken with Senator Hickman since the introduction of this language, I understand that he is amenable to an amendment to the bill updating the amount to be transferred to the fund biannually to a more up-to-date $410,000. I appreciate his flexibility.

Section two of the bill re-establishes a working group to, among other duties, investigate the feasibility of using schools as voting places around the State of Maine. This is not a conversation we are new to -- in fact we've been convening meetings on this topic for a couple years now -- but we have not gotten to a point of having a conclusion to present to you and would like to continue this work in a formal manner. These are weighty matters. Our lack of conclusions at this point is not due to a lack of effort,
but simply that there are no easy answers. There are several important and laudable goals from all, which are sometimes in friction with each other. Section two would allow a formal working group to continue to meet through the rest of this year and provide a report to you in December.
This concludes my testimony. Thank you and I would be happy to answer any questions that the committee may have.

The Secretary of State's decision to provide funds necessary for the production and delivery of election materials is a commendable step towards ensuring fair and efficient elections. By allocating resources to this important aspect of the electoral process, the Secretary of State is demonstrating a commitment to upholding democracy and promoting voter participation.
Furthermore, the decision to reconvene the Working Group to study polling places at schools shows a willingness to address potential logistical challenges and improve the voting experience for all citizens. By actively seeking input and feedback from stakeholders, the Secretary of State is taking a proactive approach to ensuring that polling places are convenient and accessible to all voters.
Overall, the Secretary of State's actions reflect a high level of creativity and dedication to improving the electoral process. By prioritizing the production and delivery of election materials and addressing issues related to polling places, the Secretary of State is demonstrating a commitment to promoting transparency, efficiency, and inclusivity in the electoral process.
